details.publicNotes:
Weather vanes are useful ways of telling direction with the wind. Occasionally a stray bolt of lightning connects with one, and even rarer, the weather vane absorbs not just the electricity, but a storm spirit as well. Once the storm spirit realizes they have become trapped in a metal prison, they lash out at anyone with the misfortune to come nearby. With deadly bolts of electricity and powerful gales, they attempt to keep others from approaching their newly immobile form.

Unfortunately for weatherbanes, unless someone manages to push through their storms and destroy their metal bodies, they are doomed to remain trapped. If someone does manage this deed, the spirit bears no grudge toward them and might even offer them a minor boon before taking to the skies once more.

Songs of the Storm

When a weatherbane is topped by the image of a creature such as a rooster, the weather spirit embodies that creature, and its sound can be heard echoing from rooftops for miles around. Weatherbane-haunted villages ring with the crows of roosters, the clop of horses' hooves, or the roars of dragons. In seaside towns, weatherbanes might instead emit songs similar to those of whales or sirens.

Suggested Monster Parts

Monster Parts 7/18/30 gp

Eligible Refinements weapons (bludgeoning), perception item, skill items (Intimidation, Nature)

Eligible Imbued Properties air, bane, charisma, dexterity, electricity, elongating, energy resistant (electricity, sonic, spirit, vitality, void), intelligence, sensory (darkvision), throwing, wild, wisdom

description.value:
Trigger The weatherbane is the target of a physical ranged attack

Requirements The weatherbane is aware of the attack and not @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.AJh5ex99aV6VTggg]{Off-Guard}

Effect The weatherbane gains a +4 circumstance bonus to AC against the triggering attack.

With a smell of ozone, the weatherbane calls for the might of the storm. They attempt an electrobolt Strike. If the Strike hits, the target and any creatures within a @Template[type:emanation|distance:15] around the target take @Damage[1d6[electricity]|options:area-damage] damage (@Check[fortitude|dc:20|basic] save). Any creature that fails its save also takes a –10-foot status penalty to its Speeds for 1 round.

Trigger A Large or smaller creature takes damage from the weatherbane's gust Strike

Effect The weatherbane attempts to blow the creature away from them, rolling a Nature check against the creature's Fortitude DC. The creature is blown back 10 feet on a success, or 20 feet on a critical success.

The weatherbane changes the direction of the wind in a @Template[type:emanation|distance:60] until the start of their next turn. They can choose to make the wind in the entire area point in a specific direction, to draw the wind toward themselves, or to push the wind away from themselves. All Large or smaller creatures in the area must attempt a @Check[fortitude|dc:18] save. Large or smaller creatures that later enter the area while the winds persist must also attempt this save. The weatherbane can't use Wind Blast again for [[/gmr 1d4 #Recharge Wind Blast]]{1d4 rounds}.

Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature can't move against the wind.

Failure The creature is pushed 30 feet in the wind's direction and knocked @UUID[Compendium.pf2e.conditionitems.Item.j91X7x0XSomq8d60]{Prone}. If it was flying, it experiences the effects of critical failure instead.

Critical Failure The creature is pushed 60 feet in the wind's direction, knocked prone, and takes @Damage[2d6[bludgeoning]|options:area-damage] damage.

As an enraged spirit in a metal prison, a weatherbane can only spin in place. They can't move or be moved, except through teleportation or similar magical means. If a weatherbane is moved, the grounding connection is severed, freeing the spirit within and destroying the weatherbane.
